t.E512.agn: In its 2018 re-evaluation, EFSA found no concern regarding carcinogenicity or genotoxicity and concluded that there was no safety concern for the single authorised use (up to 25 mg tin/kg); no product labelled with this additive was identified in the EU. Gastrointestinal irritation has been reported in humans after a single intake of 40 mg of tin; JECFA also set a provisional tolerable weekly intake (PTWI, 1988) of 14 mg/kg body weight for tin and noted that tin levels as low as 150 mg/kg in canned beverages and 250 mg/kg in other canned foods may cause gastric irritation.
t.E512.body: Tin(II) chloride is poorly absorbed from the digestive tract.
t.E512.eff.0.a: A single dose of 40 mg tin; tin levels as low as 150 mg per kilogram in canned beverages and 250 mg in other canned foods
t.E512.prod: It is produced chemically by the reaction of tin with chlorine or hydrochloric acid.
t.E512.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no safety concern for the current authorised use.
t.E512.regx.1: Only in canned/bottled white asparagus, up to 25 mg/kg (as tin).
t.E512.regx.2: PTWI for tin of 14 mg/kg bw (including use as a food additive).
t.E512.summary: Tin chloride. Used to preserve colour in products such as canned asparagus.
t.E512.what: It is a tin salt that helps preserve colour and acts as an antioxidant; in the EU it is permitted only in canned white asparagus.
